product_delta.area: Clerk identity routing / browser authentication boundary
product_delta.defect: CLAYVERSE_CLERK_MAP_JSON admitted any non-empty mapping whose values covered gabriel and andreas, so extra Clerk subject IDs could silently alias either canonical perspective.
product_delta.repair: Require exactly two non-empty Clerk subject mappings and a bijection onto gabriel and andreas; reject extra subjects, missing users, duplicate user targets, blank subjects and foreign targets.

isolated_mechanism_evidence.scope: extracted _clerk_map logic only; not full checkout, not Vercel Sandbox, not OCI runtime

unusual_experiment.reason: No shared immutable request/turn identifier is exposed and the available exact user-message timestamp is only minute-precision (2026-08-17T13:42+07:00); GO_EXPERIMENT_ATOMIC_LEASE_PROTOCOL requires whole-second precision or stronger identity for timestamp fallback.

counterhypothesis: Multiple Clerk subjects per canonical user might be intentionally desired for account migration or alternate identities. The baseline product does not currently define such alias semantics; silently allowing aliases weakens explicit identity binding. Any future aliasing should therefore be separately typed, bounded and tested rather than inferred from a permissive map.
next_exact_gate: Run the exact then-current fused head in an actually-started authorized Vercel Sandbox: focused Clerk mapping regressions plus existing JWT/session/auth-first WebSocket tests, then broader artifact tests and exact OCI build/start/readiness with real Clerk browser/JWT behavior.
